nodes.description: A heterozygous germline TGFBR1 variant inactivates one allele in every cell. MSSE variants are nonsense, frameshift and splice variants spread through the gene, some of which abolish expression of the mutant mRNA, or missense variants in the extracellular ligand-binding domain. One functional copy is enough for normal development.

nodes.description: Biallelic TGFBR1 loss removes TGF-beta receptor signaling from the keratinocyte, and with it the growth-suppressive action TGF-beta has in normal skin. That this releases an invasive, self-limited keratinocyte tumor is inferred: the growth-suppression evidence comes from sporadic cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma and mouse skin, not from MSSE tumors themselves. The permissive second locus on 9q22.3 is also thought to be required, and how it acts is unknown.
nodes.id: Loss of TGF-beta Receptor Signaling in Keratinocytes

evidence.snippet: Inactivating mutations in transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β) receptors have been identified amongst genetic drivers of sporadic tumours and murine models of cSCC, suggesting a tumour suppressor function for TGF-β in normal skin

nodes.description: Multiple skin tumors that start as a red macule, become papular, enlarge and ulcerate, invade the dermis over a few weeks and then regress spontaneously after several months. Histologically they resemble well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma or keratoacanthoma. They arise mostly on sun-exposed skin of the head, neck and limbs, most often the nose, ears and perioral skin; the trunk is seldom affected. Lesion number ranges from one or two in a lifetime to more than 100. Age at first tumor ranges from 8 to 81 years. Distant metastasis has not been reported.

evidence.reference_title: Multiple self-healing squamous epithelioma is caused by a disease-specific spectrum of mutations in TGFBR1.

evidence.snippet: Affected patients suffer from recurrent skin lesions, which clinically and histologically resemble keratoacanthomas or well-differentiated squamous cell carcinomas, but which, if left, undergo spontaneous regression, leaving pronounced scarring.

nodes.description: Each tumor stops growing after weeks and involutes over several months. The invasive epithelial columns keratinize centrally and coalesce into a horny plug that falls out, and the base shows dermal fibrosis with loss of elastic fibers, leaving a pitted scar. Lymphocytes often infiltrate the tumors, and one regressed tumor carried more plasmacytoid dendritic cells than a mature one from the same patient, but what drives regression is not known.

evidence.snippet: Lymphocytes often infiltrate the tumors but their role in tumor resolution is not known.
